correctness.rationale: On the sum-zero hyperplane, simultaneous translation of all six coordinates fixes the equation, giving the cone over x6=0. A vanishing restricted gradient requires the six numbers s*x_i−x_i^3 to agree, with s=sum(x_i^2). If s=0, all coordinates agree; otherwise write x_i=a+r*t_i, r^2=s and t_i in F_3. The conditions sum(t_i)=0 and sum(t_i^2)=1 force the multiplicities of 1 and −1 to be 2 modulo 3 and hence both exactly 2, leaving two zeros. Affine permutations of the values identify exactly the fifteen unordered pairings. On the hyperplane the Hessian is r² times the dot product minus the rank-one form given by t; its radical is span(1,t), so the projective base has fifteen A1 nodes and no other singular points. The finite singular set also excludes either a repeated factor or geometrically distinct components. A crepant resolution is K3 by adjunction and the rationality of the A1 singularities; the exceptional conics over F_3 are split by the finite-field conic theorem. The independent enumeration replay at review-evidence/4-igusa-base-count.js uses e4−e2², last-nonzero-coordinate projective representatives, and theta²=theta+1 for F_9. It returned 25 and 145 base points, with 15 singular points over both fields. Thus the resolution counts 70 and 280 give trace power sums 60 and 198. The weight-two bound makes the second sum extremal, forcing every squared eigenvalue to be 9; the first sum fixes the signs. The cone formula 1+q·#B and the zeta formulas follow. This concerns the specified F_3 models and the geometric singular set of the cone, not arbitrary twists or an assertion about the Jacobian ideal at the cone vertex. The frozen verifier and output were inspected, not executed.
